question.text: 'Yamuna Capital AIF' PPM says a defaulting LP forfeits 25% of his contributed capital plus pays 15% default interest on the unpaid drawdown. Mr. X had contributed INR 8 crore to date and defaults on a further drawdown of INR 2 crore (due for 90 days). Ignoring rounding, what is the forfeiture amount and default interest (approx)?

answer.text: Forfeit INR 2 crore; interest INR 75 lakh
Forfeit INR 4 crore; interest INR 30 lakh
Forfeit INR 2 crore; interest approx INR 7.4 lakh (for 90 days)

explanation.text: The Logic: Forfeit = 25% x INR 8 crore already contributed = INR 2 crore. Default interest on the unpaid INR 2 crore drawdown at 15% p.a. for 90 days = 2 x 0.15 x (90/365) = INR 0.074 crore = INR 7.4 lakh approx. The Trap: INR 75 lakh forgets to pro-rate interest for 90 days. INR 30 lakh over-applies. Full expulsion is not aligned with the 25% clause. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers default arithmetic. XIX-D focuses on drafting the forfeiture vs pro-rata top-up split. Manager's Pro-Tip: Standard PPM forfeiture is tiered: interest for <30 days delay, pro-rata buyout by non-defaulters for 30-60 days, expulsion after 60+. Keep the tiers proportionate to avoid LP-manager disputes.
